results.summary_before: This design counts the number of digital pulses occurring within a time interval across four input channels. The counts are periodically output using a serial output. It is intended for low-power wake-up sensor interfaces, acoustic event detection, non-destructive testing, and particle counting. The design is a generic pulse-counting digital building block.
results.summary: This design implements the Bulls and Cows number-guessing game in Verilog. A secret pattern of four distinct 3-bit numbers is stored via a save signal, and the player enters guesses through the input pins. The design compares each guess to the secret and reports bulls (correct digit and position) and cows (correct digit, wrong position) on a seven-segment display. The goal is to reach four bulls.

results.summary_before: The design implements a neural network accelerator with fixed-point arithmetic and a spiking neural network mode. It is intended for FPGA deployment and communicates via UART. The core clock and reset come from an external FPGA through input pins, while the on-board RP2040 clock is used only for debug and mirrored to an output. The design is notable for its machine learning capabilities in a small form factor.
results.summary: This design implements the SAP-1 (Simple As Possible) 8-bit computer architecture in Verilog, forked from Brandon Cruz's design. It contains a clock, program counter, registers A and B, an adder, multiplier, divider, memory, instruction register, bus and controller. The 8-bit bus carries data between modules under load and enable control, and instruction execution proceeds through six stages. The only current way to read the bus output is with an oscilloscope.

results.summary: This project implements a stochastic integrator in Verilog using Euler's definition of integration in the stochastic domain. It follows unipolar probability and takes two serial bitstream inputs. The outputs provide several serial bitstream results for sequence, system and test integrators. Testing is done by holding one input high and the other low to observe the described equations.

results.summary: This analog design implements an 8-bit R2R DAC and a 4-bit flash ADC. The DAC inputs connect directly to the digital input pins, and its output reaches the analog pin through a transmission gate when the dac_connect pin is high. The flash ADC has a 0-1 V input range with reference voltages from a resistive divider, and its output is multiplexed onto three 4-bit buses. The ADC reference can be calibrated from the analog pin by setting adc_cal_connect high.
